__baseline_prompt__.text: A Clockpunk photograph: an everyday scene involving clockwork, centered on a fictional woman caring for a tray of herb seedlings in a small Renaissance-inspired courtyard workshop. Her facial proportions and short straight dark bob with wispy separated bangs follow the supplied appearance reference. She bends slightly over a limestone workbench, her attention caught by the first thread of water reaching a fragile seedling. Her relaxed mouth, warm skin catching the morning light, and the quiet confidence of her stance give the working portrait an intimate, unforced appeal. A soft sage linen blouse, sleeves rolled above the forearms, and a plain tied work apron belong naturally to this damp, sunlit task. Beside her stands a handmade spring-driven irrigation regulator, about the size of a bread loaf, its open brass side plate turned toward the viewer. A flat spiral steel mainspring is visible inside an open winding drum. The drum's arbor carries a small toothed pinion meshing directly with a broad brass gear. That gear's axle carries an offset wooden cam, fully visible beside the wheel. At this instant the raised cam nose lifts the underside of a short lever arm; across the central pivot, the lever's longer arm depresses the stem of a small brass water valve. The metal parts have working clearances, polished contact patches and tiny traces of green oxidation. This is clockwork in use, with the teeth, axle, cam contact and valve connection readable as one practical assembly. A small terracotta reservoir is raised on a timber bracket above the mechanism. A single copper feed tube runs down from its bottom into the valve, and a short downstream spout sends one fine continuous stream onto the soil at the front of the seed tray. The soil immediately around that landing point is visibly darker than the dry soil farther away. Her right fingertips rest lightly on the regulator's winding key at its near side, clear of the gear teeth; her left hand steadies the front rim of the wooden tray, with each wrist connected to its own visible forearm. Her gaze follows the landing water rather than the camera. Photograph from close three-quarter bench height with a normal lens, including her face, both hands, the whole regulator, the reservoir and the water's landing point. Keep these relationships within a generous shared focus plane. The face, spring mechanism and watered seedling form a descending visual triangle. Low morning sun rakes the brass and outlines the bob; soft courtyard bounce preserves the eyes. Worn stone, restrained leafy shadows and one folded cloth make an inhabited setting, with the mechanism's purposeful movement and her attention carrying the frame. Natural photographic texture and restrained warm color.
